read_scope.notes: Read all 22 PDF pages, including the abstract, main text, references and Appendices A–G. Inspected full-page PDF renderings of every page, including Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–10. Consulted frozen paper.tex and specificity_results.tex for notation and exact locations. Technical appendix material was treated as optional depth. No other reviews or manuscript versions were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with useful concrete explanations. The opening Monet/Sisley example explains why collection proximity is insufficient; Section 4.1 then explains centering and the 1/0/1 error benchmarks without relying on equations. Qualifications are generally tied to the inference they limit, especially in Sections 5.4–5.5. The occasional switch between aligned response and slope is a localized terminology refinement rather than a pervasive clarity problem.
score_reasons.structure: The main narrative stands on its own: motivation and design lead to an interpretable feature table, score intuition, primary comparisons, and clearly marked retrospective diagnostics. Result headings state what each analysis reveals. Table 3 makes calibration and scene averaging distinguishable; Table 4 makes changed source-corrected comparisons explicit. Appendix placement successfully preserves estimator derivations, complete comparisons and earlier cohorts without requiring them to reconstruct the main argument. No consequential restructuring is needed.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The abstract identifies the design, finite digital target, major numerical result, unresolved benchmark comparison and perceptual limit. The prompt clauses and repeats are explicit; development-IQR units are explained; the lightness example and expected-error benchmarks make the central measures interpretable. The principal remaining friction is local to the mathematical notation in Section 4.2 and the unexplained naming change from aligned response to slope. Figure 2 is interpretable but could key its faint individual-output markers more explicitly.
score_reasons.engagement: The question has a clear consequence for evaluating generators, and the narrative develops through revealing contrasts: positive alignment without low error, weak Monet/Sisley distinctions, and model ordering changes under calibration or scene averaging. Figure 1 supplies a concrete common-scene comparison, Figure 2 magnifies the otherwise crowded painter means, and Figure 3 makes pair asymmetry immediately inspectable. The paper sustains attention through explanations of what the numbers reveal, with little hype. Remaining refinements concern local labeling rather than a missing narrative.

strengths: Section 4.1, page 5, gives both an observed lightness gap and idealized errors of 1, 0 and 1; this is an effective bridge from the research question to beta and D.
Sections 3.1–3.3 explain the finite reference collection, equal painter weighting, exact intervention arms and feature units while distinguishing digital texture from physical brushwork.
Section 5.1 and Table 2 distinguish detecting alignment from establishing improvement over the no-contrast benchmark, and report that only two original model-pair comparisons are resolved.
Section 5.4 and Table 3 turn calibration and scene dependence into concrete model comparisons while stating that rescaling features does not create improved images.
Section 5.5 and Table 4 preserve the original results and visibly identify which intervals change after source correction; the AI audit and retrospective status are explicit.
Figures 1–3 offer complementary inspection routes: actual outputs and controls, labeled reference/generated geometry, and fully annotated pair scores.

findings.issue: The transition from the accessible lightness example to the score equations introduces norm bars, angle brackets and estimate hats without a short notation key. H is described only as setting the error scale. Readers unfamiliar with this statistical notation must infer how the coordinate products become an overall score.
findings.reader_effect: The central equations are more intimidating than their underlying operations, even though the surrounding prose provides enough intuition to continue reading.
findings.suggested_change: Replace “H sets the error scale” with a brief statement that H sums squared reference contrasts, and explain once that angle brackets multiply matching coordinates and sum them, while hats denote estimates. Keep the affine-transformation caveat in plain language and move its algebra to Appendix B if needed to accommodate these words within the existing page count.

findings.location: Sections 4.1, 4.3 and 5.3–5.4, pages 5–9; paper.tex lines 224–226 and 280; specificity_results.tex lines 68–70 and 91–95
findings.issue: Beta is introduced as the “aligned response,” then called an “aligned-response slope,” an “overall slope” and an “aligned slope” without explicitly linking those names. Figure 3 also uses “Pair slope.”
findings.reader_effect: A new reader can briefly wonder whether the slope is a further regression statistic rather than the same normalized projection, especially when moving from the overall result to artist pairs.
findings.suggested_change: Use “aligned response” consistently in the main text and “Pair aligned response beta” in Figure 3, or add “also called the projection slope” at the first definition. This can be a word-neutral replacement.

findings.location: Figure 2 and caption, page 7; specificity_results.tex lines 31–36
findings.issue: The legend explicitly keys reference crosses and generated-mean circles, but the numerous faint overview dots are only indirectly explained by “retains all scene/repeat points.”
findings.reader_effect: Readers scanning the figure can mistake the faint cloud for uncertainty around a mean or fail to distinguish individual outputs from the mean markers.
findings.suggested_change: Key “faint dots: individual scene/repeat outputs” in the existing legend, or replace the caption sentence with “Faint dots show individual scene/repeat outputs; open circles show their means.” Use the existing figure area and caption space.

summary: An excellent, self-contained editorial presentation of a bounded comparison of digital painter contrasts. Its core distinctions, principal findings and uncertainty are readily recoverable, and the appendices supply optional technical depth. Only localized notation and figure-label refinements are needed; no new evidence or additional pages are warranted.
